subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw extend the stable status/usage JSON contract with per-session agent, cron, and channel attribution fields, and where should that contract live?
rationale: Current main has partial attribution across status, sessions.usage, and cron APIs, but the requested stable row shape affects public JSON/API semantics and privacy for channel identifiers.

options.title: Extend sessions.usage as the canonical export
options.body: Add documented optional agent/session kind/cron/channel/model/runtime fields to sessions.usage and let status JSON point dashboards there instead of duplicating joins.

options.title: Add a distinct usage attribution export
options.body: Keep status --usage provider-focused and introduce a separate export/RPC for dashboard attribution if maintainers want a clearer contract boundary.

options.title: Defer and keep local adapters
options.body: Leave the request open or close as not planned if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own dashboard attribution beyond current surfaces.

recommendation.title: Extend sessions.usage as the canonical export
recommendation.body: Add documented optional agent/session kind/cron/channel/model/runtime fields to sessions.usage and let status JSON point dashboards there instead of duplicating joins.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to status JSON helper ownership and recent status-surface work among the traced owners.
